title: tmp file deletion (not quarantine) is semantically correct
description: cleanup_tmp_files deletes .msg.tmp and .env.tmp files rather than moving them to dead/. This is semantically correct: a .tmp file represents an in-progress atomic write that never completed the rename step, so no committed record ever existed. There is no data to recover. A future contributor might suggest 'why not move to dead/ for operator inspection' — the answer is that there is nothing useful in a partial write: the content was never committed, and moving it to dead/ would pollute the dead/ queue with unrecoverable artifacts. The doc comment in the source explains this correctly.
